name: Graphify-Labs/graphify
reviewed_by: Kit 3 registry pass - gates applied, source not yet read
verdict_summary: Fails `collisions`: ships a PreToolUse hook that intercepts file-search tool calls, and in strict mode blocks the first raw source read of a session. That is the same interception point our own local-context.sh occupies, and no precedence resolution has been recorded. Fails `measurability` and `maintenance_ownership` independently. Four further gates are unknown because the source and install script have not been read. Rejection is on architecture and process, not on capability - the retrieval claim is credible and worth a bake-off (see intersection_map).

install.command: graphify install --project   (strict mode adds --strict; both write a CLAUDE.md directive and a PreToolUse hook into the target)
install.notes: Registry never runs this. A human runs it after reading the install path in full.

license.evidence: Apache-2.0, confirmed via GitHub API 2026-08-31. Permissive, compatible with client work-for-hire terms.

data_egress.evidence: Upstream claims local-first deterministic AST parsing with no external API calls for parsing and no vector store. That claim covers parsing only; it says nothing about telemetry, update checks, or crash reporting. Source not read.
data_egress.resolves_by: Read the CLI and hook source for outbound network calls; confirm whether any usage/telemetry ping exists and whether it can be disabled.

pinning.evidence: Public git repository with versioned branches (v8 observed), so an exact SHA is available in principle. Whether the documented `graphify install` path accepts a pinned ref, or resolves a floating latest at install time, has not been confirmed.
pinning.resolves_by: Confirm the CLI installs from a pinnable ref; if it does not, fork and install from the fork.

uninstall.evidence: Install writes at least two artifacts into the target (a CLAUDE.md directive and a PreToolUse hook) plus graph data. No uninstall command has been confirmed, and residue after removal is unmeasured.
uninstall.resolves_by: Confirm an uninstall path exists that removes the hook, the CLAUDE.md directive, and the built graph, leaving the client repository as it was.

collisions.evidence: Architectural collision at the PreToolUse boundary. Graphify's Claude Code integration installs a PreToolUse hook that intercepts file-search tool calls before they run, and its strict mode blocks the first raw source read of a session outright to force graph use. Our editions already occupy PreToolUse with local-context.sh, and Symfony additionally gates Agent|Task through subagent-gate.sh. Deny-wins means neither hook can weaken the other, but two enforcement systems both refusing a call is a live failure mode, not a theoretical one - and the ordering between them is undefined. No precedence resolution is recorded.
collisions.resolves_by: Record a hook-precedence resolution: which hook runs first, what happens when both would block, and whether strict mode is permitted at all. Test on a throwaway branch against the current Claude Code version before the resolution is treated as real.

auto_update.evidence: Not confirmed whether the installed CLI or hook self-updates, or whether the graph rebuild path pulls new upstream code.
auto_update.resolves_by: Read the install script and CLI for any self-update or version-check-and-fetch behaviour.

maintenance_ownership.evidence: No owner assigned. 1,164 open issues at review time, and no relationship with the maintainer. If the hook breaks a client's session mid-engagement, there is currently no named person whose ticket it is.
maintenance_ownership.resolves_by: Either name an internal owner who will fork and carry it, or do not install. Forking makes the answer 'us' and is a deliberate, priced choice.

measurability.evidence: Cost is unmeasured on our own ruler. Upstream cites a 71.5x per-query token reduction on a ~92,000-word corpus, which is a vendor claim about a different corpus, not a measurement of what a client engagement would pay. The one-time graph build is reported in hours and incremental rebuild around ten minutes - both unverified, and neither expressed in the startup/per-invocation split that scripts/context_budget.py produces for our own editions.
measurability.resolves_by: Extend scripts/context_budget.py with an external-tree mode, then measure the installed surface (CLAUDE.md directive + hook) as startup cost and the graph-query path as per-invocation cost.

automation_depth.evidence: Fully self-orchestrating once installed: the hook fires on every file-search tool call without invocation, and strict mode actively redirects reads. Maximum depth means maximum consequence - this is the reason for scrutiny, not a reason to prefer it.

token_efficiency.evidence: Unmeasured on our ruler. Scores 0 by rule, which is also what fails the measurability gate. Not a claim that it is inefficient - upstream's claimed direction is plausible - only that we have no number of our own.

integration_coverage.evidence: Targets Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and Gemini CLI. Covers all three of our supported integrations, though the deepest integration (hook-based) is Claude Code only, so coverage is not uniform.

trust_signals.evidence: Active: last push 2026-08-30, ~1,629 commits on the v8 branch, permissive license, substantial documentation. Against: 1,164 open issues is a large backlog for a five-month-old project; bus factor, issue response time, release/semver discipline and test coverage are all unassessed; the install path writes an enforcement hook into the target, which is the highest-consequence artifact a third party can add.
disqualified_signals: star count: 112,842 stars / 10,980 forks at ~5 months old (created 2026-04-03, verified via GitHub API 2026-08-31). Statistically implausible for the age; matches the fake-star pattern in arXiv 2412.13459. Recorded, never scored.

intersection_map.detail: Both answer 'find me the relevant part of this repository' from a locally built index. Ours indexes policy, skills, docs, specs and Project Brain records; graphify indexes code structure plus docs, schemas and PDFs as a graph. The overlap is the retrieval job itself, not the data model. Until the same question set is run through both, installing both means paying twice for one job - which the memo names as the real hidden cost of Kit 3, above token cost.
Both occupy the PreToolUse interception point. Deny-wins protects correctness, but ordering is undefined and a both-block outcome is unhandled. This is what fails the collisions gate.
No overlap. Memory Bank holds durable authored knowledge with provenance; graphify holds derived structural facts about code. A graph edge is not a memory chunk and neither substitutes for the other.

lifecycle.residue: unknown - at minimum a CLAUDE.md directive, a PreToolUse hook, and the built graph artifacts; none confirmed removable

open_questions: Does the same query set answered by the Local Context Engine get materially better answers from the graph? If not, this is a duplicate, not a kit.
What is the real one-time build cost on a client-sized monorepo, and what is the staleness policy - rebuild on demand, nightly, or per change?
Can the PreToolUse hook be installed in non-strict mode only, and does that still deliver the retrieval benefit?
